text: {"score":2,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (9.6%, 1.8%, 5.05, z 0.70, 71%, 45 records, 17 documented 99215 with 1 below, 5 of 37). But the narrative is internally inconsistent and cites claims that do not support the sentences. The headline says the charts largely support billing and leaves the pattern unresolved, yet the rationale says 'the claims pattern points toward upcoding.' It also names a claim that is not on the card and asserts diagnoses and note signals the evidence cannot support.","problems":["Internal contradiction: 'points toward upcoding' vs headline and leaning 'inconclusive' with charts largely supporting billed levels.","C0045994 is cited as a flagged note to pull but does not appear anywhere on the evidence card; it is unsupported/fabricated.","The 36% 'problems' note-sign figure is not on the card and could not be matched by the script; the summary also does not show it comes from a tool output.","The claim that 'time entries repeat in some notes' has no support on the card.","The sampled diagnoses list 'rash' and 'URI', but the cited claims show no rash diagnosis (J06.9 is URI; R21 is the rash code, not named in the claims). C0046056 is R21, C0046072 is Z09. The 'routine' characterization is loosely supported.","Example C0046453 is in the below-billed documentation list but is also a low-complexity 99215 claim. It is used as an example without explaining that it is the single below-billed chart.","The z-score of 0.70 vs peers is only mentioned, not interpreted. It weakens the 'far above' framing, which rests on the risk-adjusted score.","Next steps are generic: they repeat the already cited claims and do not specify which documentation to request for high-complexity versus low-complexity claims."]}
